Compute the numbers of a descriptive table

Source: R/table1.R
table1.Rd

table1() computes the numbers of a descriptive table, per group and for all rows. With a style, it also formats these numbers as text.

Usage

table1(d, by, vars, style = NULL)

Arguments

d

A data.table, or a data.frame.

by

The name of the grouping column in d.

vars

A data.table with the columns var and type. var names a column in d. type is "bin" for a 0/1 variable, or "cont" for a numeric variable.

style

NULL, the name of an installed style, or the path to a style file that ends in .yml. table1_styles() gives the names of the installed styles. With NULL, table1() does no formatting. The section Styles below describes a style file.

Value

A data.table with one row per variable and group, in the order of vars, and "All" first. The columns are var, grp, n, missing, mean, sd, events, pct, p and test. n counts the non-missing values. With a style, the columns value_pretty (the cell text) and p_pretty (the text of p) follow. The attribute footnotes then holds the footnotes of the style as a character vector. The other columns are the same as with style = NULL.

Details

The groups are the levels of by, plus "All". The levels are the factor levels when by is a factor, and the sorted unique values otherwise. A row with a missing by counts in "All" only. A level of by that is "All" is an error. A level with no rows has a row in the output with n = 0.

For a "bin" variable:

  • events is the count of 1, and pct is 100 * events / n.

  • p compares the levels of by that have a non-missing value. It comes from the Pearson chi-square test without continuity correction. When any expected count is below 5, it comes from Fisher's exact test.

  • test is "chisq" or "fisher", and it is the same on every row of the variable. When fewer than two levels have a non-missing value, p and test are NA.

  • A value other than 0, 1 or NA is an error.

For a "cont" variable, mean and sd hold the numbers. p and test are NA in this version.

A column that does not apply to the type holds NA.

Styles

A style formats the numbers of table1() for a journal or a report. A style can only format what table1() computes. It cannot add a median, an IQR or a test of a "cont" variable.

An installed style is the file inst/table1/<name>_<YYYY_MM_DD>.yml of pbn. Its name is the file name without .yml. pbn never edits a released style, so a changed style gets a new date.

A style file is a YAML map of sections. Each field of a section is a map with the keys value and source. source is one string that says where the value comes from. Examples are the guide and its count of papers (k/N papers), the guideline and its page, and editorial choice. table1() checks every field when it reads the file. An unknown field, a missing field, a missing source or a value that the field does not allow stops it. The error names the field and the file.

A template is text with placeholders in braces, such as {events}. A template can hold only the placeholders of its field, in any order, and it can hold none. These are the fields:

  • bin.template: the cell of a "bin" row, over {events}, {n} and {pct}. An example is "{events} ({pct})".

  • bin.pct_digits: the decimals of pct, a whole number from 0 to 10.

  • cont.template: the cell of a "cont" row, over {mean} and {sd}.

  • cont.mean_digits and cont.sd_digits: the decimals of mean and of sd, each a whole number from 0 to 10.

  • p.digits: the decimals of p, a whole number from 0 to 10.

  • p.template: the text of p, over {p}. "P ={p}" gives P =0.005, and "{p}" gives the number only.

  • p.lower: null, or a number above 0 and below 1. A p below it gets p.below_template in place of p.template.

  • p.below_template: the text of such a p, over {lower}. With p.lower 0.001, "P <{lower}" gives P <0.001.

  • p.upper: null, or a number above 0 and below 1. A p above it gets p.above_template.

  • p.above_template: the text of such a p, over {upper}. With p.upper 0.999, "P >{upper}" gives P >0.999.

  • thousands.mark: the thousands separator, such as ",". The empty string "" gives no separator.

  • thousands.from: a number above 0. A number gets the separator when its rounded absolute value is thousands.from or more. With 10000, 12347 prints as 12,347 and 9999 prints as 9999.

  • missing.show: never, if_any or always. With if_any, a cell gets missing.template when missing is above 0.

  • missing.template: the text that table1() adds to the end of a cell, over {missing}. An example is "; {missing} missing".

  • footnotes: a list, which can be empty. Each item is a map with the keys value and source, and value is the text of one footnote.

p.lower and p.upper print with p.digits decimals, so each MUST have no more decimals than p.digits. p.lower MUST be below p.upper. table1() compares p with the thresholds before it rounds p, so 0.9994 is above 0.999. A p equal to a threshold gets p.template.

table1() rounds each number with formatC(), which rounds as the C function sprintf() does. events, n and missing print with no decimals. The thousands separator applies to every number of a cell. A cell is NA when a number of its template is NA, as for a group with n = 0. p_pretty is NA where p is NA.

See also

Other shared helpers: table1_styles()

Examples

d <- data.table::data.table(
  g = rep(c("a", "b"), each = 10),
  smoker = rep(c(1, 0, 0, 1), 5),
  age = 21:40
)
vars <- data.table::data.table(
  var = c("smoker", "age"),
  type = c("bin", "cont")
)
pbn::table1(d, by = "g", vars = vars)
#>       var    grp     n missing  mean      sd events   pct     p   test
#>    <char> <char> <int>   <int> <num>   <num>  <int> <num> <num> <char>
#> 1: smoker    All    20       0    NA      NA     10    50     1  chisq
#> 2: smoker      a    10       0    NA      NA      5    50     1  chisq
#> 3: smoker      b    10       0    NA      NA      5    50     1  chisq
#> 4:    age    All    20       0  30.5 5.91608     NA    NA    NA   <NA>
#> 5:    age      a    10       0  25.5 3.02765     NA    NA    NA   <NA>
#> 6:    age      b    10       0  35.5 3.02765     NA    NA    NA   <NA>

# A style file, written to tempdir()
style <- file.path(tempdir(), "example_2026_12_01.yml")
writeLines(c(
  "bin:",
  "  template: {value: '{events} ({pct})', source: editorial choice}",
  "  pct_digits: {value: 1, source: editorial choice}",
  "cont:",
  "  template: {value: '{mean} ({sd})', source: editorial choice}",
  "  mean_digits: {value: 1, source: editorial choice}",
  "  sd_digits: {value: 1, source: editorial choice}",
  "p:",
  "  digits: {value: 3, source: editorial choice}",
  "  template: {value: 'P ={p}', source: editorial choice}",
  "  lower: {value: 0.001, source: editorial choice}",
  "  below_template: {value: 'P <{lower}', source: editorial choice}",
  "  upper: {value: 0.999, source: editorial choice}",
  "  above_template: {value: 'P >{upper}', source: editorial choice}",
  "thousands:",
  "  mark: {value: ',', source: editorial choice}",
  "  from: {value: 10000, source: editorial choice}",
  "missing:",
  "  show: {value: if_any, source: editorial choice}",
  "  template: {value: '; {missing} missing', source: editorial choice}",
  "footnotes:",
  "  - {value: 'Values are n (percent) or mean (SD).', source: editorial choice}"
), style)
t1 <- pbn::table1(d, by = "g", vars = vars, style = style)
t1[, c("var", "grp", "value_pretty", "p_pretty")]
#>       var    grp value_pretty p_pretty
#>    <char> <char>       <char>   <char>
#> 1: smoker    All    10 (50.0) P >0.999
#> 2: smoker      a     5 (50.0) P >0.999
#> 3: smoker      b     5 (50.0) P >0.999
#> 4:    age    All   30.5 (5.9)     <NA>
#> 5:    age      a   25.5 (3.0)     <NA>
#> 6:    age      b   35.5 (3.0)     <NA>
attr(t1, "footnotes")
#> [1] "Values are n (percent) or mean (SD)."
